### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**2** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts.template`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts.template`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **143** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8baeda52096bf2caf7007ceb8dd88735fe455ac8` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `beb8e229e41a77298b7e172f537e22045852f298` — the merge of head `3d635d4cc837880fba1c37944321d541be264557` into base `8baeda52096bf2caf7007ceb8dd88735fe455ac8`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin beb8e229e41a77298b7e172f537e22045852f298 && git checkout beb8e229e41a77298b7e172f537e22045852f298
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8baeda52096bf2caf7007ceb8dd88735fe455ac8 3d635d4cc837880fba1c37944321d541be264557 && git checkout -B drift-repro 8baeda52096bf2caf7007ceb8dd88735fe455ac8 && git merge --no-ff 3d635d4cc837880fba1c37944321d541be264557

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8baeda52096bf2caf7007ceb8dd88735fe455ac8
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3d635d4cc837880fba1c37944321d541be264557`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.ui-page-panel-children-cross-references-judged.ts, .changeset/24349-page-walk-panel-children.md + .changeset/24190-line-items-hydrated-check.md, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.ui-record-line-items-props-closed.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts.template, packages/spec/src/stack-page-walk-panels.test.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts (the `componentSlot` marks and `pageComponentSlotPositions`), packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts and packages/spec/src/conversions/walk.ts (the two sibling spec walks), packages/lint/src/page-walk.ts and packages/lint/src/validate-responsive-styles.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.ui-object-master-detail-form-details-closed.ts and 18.inline-grid-column-identity-only-currency-scale-refused.ts (sibling shape), packages/spec/src/migrations/types.ts, scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, .github/workflows/pr-automation.yml (route 0), the four in-repo producers the PR names, and objectui at the console pin `0707b4ae3`: packages/components/src/renderers/layout/containers.tsx (`PageTabsRenderer`, `PageAccordionRenderer`) and packages/types/src/node-slots.ts. Face: schema, a narrowing of what `defineStack` accepts. Net diff read against merge base `71fa166e9`: 7 files, +415/-20, no generated artefact among them.

### ① Derived judgments

The one code change is the panel loop in `forEachPageComponent` (`stack.zod.ts:2424-2451`): after the unchanged direct-array rule, it descends every position of `pageComponentSlotPositions()` that carries a `panelKey` and is not `retired`, reading `props[key]` as a list of panel records and visiting only each record's `panelKey` array. Today that list is exactly one position, `items[].children`, derived from the `componentSlot` marks on `PageTabsProps.items[].children` (`component.zod.ts:997`) and `PageAccordionProps.items[].children` (`:2726`); the direct marks (`children` `:587` `:1047`, `footer` `:1069`, retired `body` `:1057`) carry no `panelKey` and are untouched by the loop. Each accept-set change this implies, judged against what the renderer at the pin draws:

- **An inline action with a `type: 'modal'` target naming no declared page, or a `type: 'flow'` target naming no declared flow, inside a `page:tabs` or `page:accordion` item's `children`** — accepted on base, refused now with `STACK_CROSS_REFERENCE_INVALID` 422 and the region-level sentence located through the panel (`regions.0.components.0.properties.items.1.children.0`). RIGHT. `PageTabsRenderer` draws `renderChildren(item.children)` (containers.tsx:989) and `PageAccordionRenderer` draws the same inside `AccordionContent` (:1189); objectui's own slot table says `items[].children` for both (node-slots.ts:157-158). The consumer at `stack.zod.ts:4126-4143` judges both halves (`flow` against `flowNames`, `modal` against `pageNames`), so the entry's and changeset's two-target claim is the code's. The guards that judge a target only when the stack declares at least one flow, or at least one page, and the modal-names-a-page-only rule are the region-level ones, unchanged.
- **An identity-only column carrying `scale` over a `currency` child field, on a `record:line_items` block's `columns` or an `object-master-detail-form` block's `details[].columns`, inside a panel** — accepted on base, refused now with the column schema's own message at the panel path. RIGHT: `collectHydratedInlineColumnErrors` (`:3673-3691`) reads both carriers through the same walk; the child-object resolution (`lineItemsChildObject`) and the must-be-declared-in-this-stack rule are unchanged.
- **Depth and roots.** A panel inside a container, under a slot, or tabs inside an accordion panel — all reached, because the loop recurses through `visitComponent` from every root the walk already had. RIGHT; the test pins each against its region-level twin with only the path changed.
- **A custom component type composing `items[].children`** — now judged, matched by shape. RIGHT and required for consistency: the exported `walkAddressedPageComponents` (`i18n-resolver.ts:2339-2367`), the conversion walker (`conversions/walk.ts:304-329`) and lint's `walkPageComponents` (`page-walk.ts:132-178`) all match a position by shape on every component, and the `pageComponentSlotPositions` docblock says every walk reads that one list and keeps none of its own.
- **Retired positions excluded** (`!retired`). RIGHT: that is the authoring-walk rule the exported walk and lint's walk apply; the conversion walker alone reads retired positions, for stored documents. Today no panel position is retired, so the filter is inert and correct by construction.
- **What does not change verdict**, each pinned by a control in the test: a panel record's own keys (an `action` on the item is not a component); a `children` list holding no component; an `object-master-detail-form` `details[]` entry carrying a `type` key and a `children` list (the direct-array rule treats it as a component node and stops at it for want of `properties`, on base and head alike; the renderer draws nothing from it); a panel-shaped list under an undeclared key; an undeclared key inside a declared panel. RIGHT: `PageTabsRenderer` and `PageAccordionRenderer` read nothing else on an item as components (the `:587` candidate helper only counts badges).
- **The direct-array rule is unchanged**, including its reach into any component-shaped array under `properties` and into the retired `page:card.body`. Narrowing it would have moved verdicts outside the card; leaving it is right, and the acceptance note says so accurately.
- **Doors.** No HTTP handler or metadata save path names `STACK_CROSS_REFERENCE_INVALID`, `collectInlinePageActions` or `collectHydratedInlineColumnErrors` outside `stack.zod.ts` (grep over every package `src`, non-test: zero hits), and the error class docblock (`:3131-3134`) records the same. The region-level refusal is reached only through `defineStack` — `os validate` (`validate.ts:240` `loadConfig` evaluates the config's default export, and a throw there is the command's refusal), `os build`, the serve/migrate host configs and `DevPlugin`. The panel refusal is reached at exactly those doors and no other; the save door runs neither on base nor on head, so there is no door the region-level one reaches that the panel one misses.
- **Order and paths.** Direct arrays are visited before panel lists on one node, matching the walks' arbitrated order; the dot-separated path form matches the direct rule's; a node is never visited twice (a panel record visited as a component by the direct rule has its `children` read only by the panel rule, since the direct rule descends only under `properties`).
- **Producers.** The four in-repo pages that nest components under a panel (showcase project detail; `sys-user`; `sys-organization`; `sys-approval-request`) carry no modal or flow target and no `scale` key; the showcase `record:line_items` block declares a `type` on every column, so the identity-only rule has nothing to judge there. The published skills carry zero `page:tabs` or `page:accordion` hits against one `page:card` control file. No producer edit was owed. RIGHT.

Prime Directive #10, sentence by sentence: the re-trued walk docblock names the three readers of the list by name; the inline-action docblock's "every root, every nesting, a `page:tabs` or `page:accordion` item's `children` included" and the grid-column docblock's line-items bullet now describe the code; the line-items entry reason ("wherever a page carries it — in a page region's components, in a container's component children, in a `page:tabs` or `page:accordion` item's `children` and in a slot") is true, its dated population sentence was already free of "not yet judged"; the master-detail sibling's "reaches the block wherever a page carries it" (entry `:46`, template `:3092`) was false on base and is true now, correctly left unchanged; the new entry's `surface`, `reason` and `acceptanceCriteria` claim the reach the code has, name `defineStack` and `objectstack validate` as the doors, and say no conversion is registered, which is true. No sentence claims the save door or the load path.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec: minor`, a `!` title, a BREAKING banner, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, one `adr-0087` marker in the `registered` form naming `ui-page-panel-children-cross-references-judged`, and a FROM → TO table with the one-line fix. That is the repo's launch-window convention for an accept-set narrowing: `check-changeset-no-major` on this head prints "direction arm: `narrowing` — a BREAKING change; during the launch window it ships `minor`" and "no `major` bump", and route 1 of the Check Changeset workflow says breaking-ness is carried by the banner plus the disposition, not the level. The changeset matches what the diff publishes: the only published change is the narrowed accept set of `defineStack` and the new semantic entry; no key, export or stored shape is added, removed or renamed.

Disposition: a semantic entry is the right form, not a bare marker. `not-required (already-registered …)` could not cover the inline-action half — no step-18 entry records the dangling modal/flow target refusal (the eight entries naming page actions are about action rows and url schemes; `dashboard-header-modal-target-page-only` is a dashboard surface) — and `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is refused on a body that frames a rewrite, which this FROM → TO table does. The entry is a refusal-only D3 record, which is the shape of its siblings (`ui-object-master-detail-form-details-closed`, `inline-grid-column-identity-only-currency-scale-refused`, `ui-record-line-items-props-closed`: id, surface, replacement, reason, acceptanceCriteria, no `conversionIds`, no `relevantWhen`; 380 of 402 step-18 entries omit `relevantWhen`). Its `STEP18_RATIONALE` fragment sits in id order between `ui-page-action-row-navigation-executor-refused` and `ui-record-json-retired`, as the list's sort-by-id rule requires; `order` values are not unique by design. `check-adr-0087-registration` on this head: "1 declared-breaking changeset(s), each carrying an ADR-0087 disposition … registered ui-page-panel-children-cross-references-judged (new here: …)". Agreed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`Check Changeset` red (three runs on this head, all `failure`).** Read in the job log of each: the only red step is `check-empty-changeset`'s foreign-changeset rule on `.changeset/24190-line-items-hydrated-check.md` ("present on the merge base and CHANGED by this PR"), the DELIBERATE CORRECTION class; in the same job `check-adr-0087-registration` and `check-changeset-no-major` pass. That is the only reason it is red. Route 0 asks for the confirmation on the PR naming the note and what changed under it, no `skip-changeset` label, and the check left red; the PR body's "Pending release note corrected" section does that, the label list carries no `skip-changeset`, and this record is the written confirmation: lines 15 and 28 of that note are now true at the release both notes share (line 15 names the panel reach "since #24349"; line 28 keeps its dated reading on `ec749fbb44` and drops "so not yet judged"), and nothing else in it changed — the net diff carries exactly those two hunks; frontmatter, `Clause-②`, marker, table and figures are byte-identical. - **Deviation (1), `registry.ts.template` outside the claim's file list.** Answered: the claim's disposition item owes the entry its `STEP18_RATIONALE` fragment, and the template is that fragment's one home; the line-items fragment's re-true is the G3 instruction applied to the same sentence in its second carrier.
- **Deviation (2), merges of `origin/main` through `os-regen-merge.sh` with nothing to regenerate.** Answered: the net diff against the merge base holds no generated artefact and no file outside the seven the PR names.
- **Deviation (3), a model-identifier trailer amended before the first push.** Answered from the remote: the seven pushed commits carry the model-free trailer pair (8 trailer lines, 0 model identifiers).
- **Round-1 deviations (container restart, `check:type-check-debt` first, worktree recreated).** Procedural, no bearing on the diff; the final-head gate readings are the PR's record and CI's are read below.
- **Acceptance note: `validateResponsiveStyles` keeps its own walk.** Verified: `validate-responsive-styles.ts:98-103,177,193-197` descends `children` / `properties.children` / `body` / `properties.body` from `regions[].components[]` only — no slots, no `footer`, no panels. The note is accurate and this PR is right not to touch `packages/lint`. ESCALATED to the seat as a finding outside this claim: that rule keeps a list of its own, which the `pageComponentSlotPositions` docblock forbids, and a `responsiveStyles` node in a tab, a card footer or a slot escapes the five style rules at `os lint`. It is reproducible from the code and is the same class as this card; it owes a `domain:spec` card with its lint rider rather than a note. Not a FAIL item here — pre-existing, outside the claim, not introduced by this diff.

Not an accept-set claim.
- **PR body: a page whose tabs item contains the tabs node itself terminates on both base and head.** Not re-measured here (read-only); unreachable from JSON or YAML metadata, and the direct-array rule carries the same exposure on base for a container that contains itself, so the class is unchanged by this diff and does not bear on the accept set.
